info.title: ERPC x402 RPC (18 chains)
info.description:
Stablecoin-gated JSON-RPC proxies plus an account-bound EURC credit top-up. POST /v1/solana-mainnet (Solana mainnet) and POST /v1/eth-mainnet (Ethereum mainnet) charge per JSON-RPC method via the x402 protocol. POST /v1/bitcoin-mainnet, /v1/polygon-mainnet, /v1/kaia-mainnet, /v1/bsc-mainnet, /v1/arbitrum-mainnet, /v1/optimism-mainnet, /v1/hyperliquid-mainnet, /v1/monad-mainnet, /v1/tron-mainnet, /v1/sui-mainnet, /v1/near-mainnet, /v1/arc-mainnet, /v1/robinhood-mainnet, /v1/soneium-mainnet, /v1/ava-mainnet and /v1/base-mainnet — the 16 other mainnet chains of the ERPC edge — charge per request method the same way, each forwarded to that chain's ERPC edge Worker over its x402 lane and priced from the chain's table (GET /pricing → <chain>.methods). Sui is sold as gRPC-web unary calls only (application/grpc-web+proto at /v1/sui-mainnet/sui.rpc.v2.<Service>/<Method>), not as JSON-RPC or GraphQL. The credit top-up sessions (/v1/credits/topup/sessions) take the account's own ERPC session as the Bearer from any caller, checked through the ERPC User API (the ERPC Dashboard calls them through the User API's /v3/user/credit-gasless-sessions): the account buys ERPC credits with EURC on Base (eip155:8453) without holding ETH, priced by the account VAT quote, receipt and credit grant issued by the ERPC receipt service. An ERPC API key is for the ERPC RPC endpoints only. Two payment rails are advertised in every 402 `accepts`: USDC on Solana (solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp) and USDC on Base (eip155:8453; EURC on Base when enabled). A rail the operator paused is listed under `howToPay.paused` instead. Ethereum L1 is never a settlement network — the Coinbase CDP facilitator cannot settle there — so the Ethereum RPC is paid for on Base or Solana. Every payment is verified and settled through the Coinbase CDP facilitator.

Registry view: account-bound credit top-up routes and the Sui root path (which rejects calls without a unary service path) are omitted. Summaries and JSON-RPC field descriptions are annotated for catalog discovery; per-call request and response schemas otherwise follow the public /doc.

post.summary: Fetch data or submit transactions on Solana mainnet
post.description: Pay-per-request Solana JSON-RPC proxy. Accepts single or batch JSON-RPC 2.0 bodies. Pricing is the per-method table of the ERPC edge (GET /pricing → solana.methods lists it): standard JSON-RPC methods cost a flat 42 tokens, getMultipleAccounts 420 per pubkey in params[0] (one pubkey when params[0] is missing, empty or not an array), DAS methods 640, getTokenLargestAccounts 2400 and getProgramAccounts 4200. Unknown methods default to 42 tokens. Calls the ERPC edge refuses as too broad (getLargestAccounts, token-program getTokenAccountsByDelegate, unfiltered getProgramAccounts on large programs, getTokenLargestAccounts on a very large mint, getMultipleAccounts with more than 100 pubkeys, and a batch that mixes heavy and light methods) are answered with HTTP 200 and a JSON-RPC error, without a payment challenge and without a charge. A batch with more than 10 getTokenLargestAccounts calls is refused the same way by this endpoint (the ERPC edge has no such cap), with -32600 for every entry. Methods this endpoint cannot serve (the ERPC gateway methods such as getTransactionsForAddress and jet*, getLeaderSlots, getValidatorsInformation and the Pyth price names) are not in /pricing and are answered the same way with JSON-RPC error -32601. Every payment is floored to a minimum charge of 1000 atomic USDC = $0.001 (the Coinbase CDP facilitator minimum settlement amount), so standard methods that would otherwise be 42 atomic ($0.000042) are charged $0.001. The first call returns 402 with an x402 payment challenge whose amount is max(summed token weight, 1000) times the base token price (1 token = $0.000001 = 1 atomic USDC, i.e. $1 per 1,000,000 tokens). The same body retried with X-Payment is settled in USDC on Solana mainnet and proxied to the upstream Solana RPC.

parameters.name: X-Payment
parameters.description: x402 payment payload (base64-encoded). Omitted on the first call, which returns 402 with an x402 challenge. On the retry the client re-sends the same JSON-RPC body with this header carrying the signed payment for the challenged amount — a Solana USDC transfer, or an EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization on Base when that rail is enabled — and the worker verifies and settles it before proxying upstream. The legacy header name Payment-Signature is also accepted as a fallback. Each settled payment is single-use within the settlement TTL — replaying it, however re-encoded or re-signed, returns 409 duplicate_payment.

200.description: Upstream JSON-RPC response. Includes X-Payment-Response header from the facilitator.

X-Payment-Response.description: Base64-encoded x402 settlement receipt for the X-Payment submitted on this request. Also mirrored as the Payment-Response header.

400.description: Invalid JSON-RPC body.

402.description: Payment Required. Returned (a) before payment with x402 challenge headers, and (b) when a submitted payment is invalid/rejected by the facilitator. The error.code is payment_required, payment_invalid, price_mismatch, settlement_failed (the facilitator reported an unsuccessful settle), or payment_amount_too_low (amount below the 1000-atomic / $0.001 facilitator minimum). Facilitator verify errors are surfaced here as a 402 rather than an HTTP 500; a settle that throws answers 502 settlement_failed unless the amount is too low. A replayed (already-used) payment is rejected separately as 409 duplicate_payment, not 402. `howToPay` tells a buyer holding none of the accepted assets where to obtain one.

post.summary: Fetch data or submit transactions on Ethereum mainnet
post.description: Pay-per-request Ethereum mainnet JSON-RPC proxy, geo-routed to the nearest ERPC Ethereum origin. Accepts single or batch JSON-RPC 2.0 bodies. Pricing uses a separate Ethereum table with the same token arithmetic as Solana: standard methods cost a flat 42 tokens (the ERPC Ethereum plan rate), eth_call / eth_estimateGas / eth_createAccessList / eth_getProof / txpool_contentFrom 420, eth_getLogs / eth_getFilterLogs / eth_getBlockReceipts / txpool_content / txpool_inspect 2400, eth_simulateV1 / eth_callMany 4200, and eth_getBlockByNumber / eth_getBlockByHash 42 with transaction hashes or 2400 with full transaction objects (params[1] === true). Batches are summed, then floored once to the 1000-atomic ($0.001) facilitator minimum. Methods outside the ERPC Ethereum catalog — including the debug_* and trace_* namespaces and the WebSocket-only eth_subscribe / eth_unsubscribe — are rejected with 400 method_not_supported BEFORE any payment is requested. The 402 challenge advertises every enabled rail (Solana USDC, Base USDC, Base EURC when enabled); the same body retried with X-Payment is settled on the rail the payer chose and proxied upstream.

post.summary: Fetch data or submit transactions on Bitcoin mainnet
post.description: Pay-per-request Bitcoin mainnet RPC over the ERPC edge Worker proxy-rpc-bitcoin, on its x402 lane (no api-key; the payment is the charge). Accepts JSON-RPC 2.0, single or batch: every call carries an id (no duplicate ids in a batch), a method matching ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ and params as an array or an object; at most 100 calls per batch and 1 MiB per body, where "jsonrpc" may also be "1.0" or omitted, at this path only. The lane's answer reaches the buyer as it is, a failure envelope included, with X-Payment-Response.

pool.description: Pool contract on Base mainnet (swap routes only), for reference. Quote through the venue router with a slippage cap; do not trade against the pool directly.

ServiceUnavailableBody.description: Returned at HTTP 503 before any payment step: no payment rail could be offered, or the worker is at its concurrency limit.

GatewayErrorBody.description: Returned at HTTP 502 and 504 when settle threw, or when the upstream call failed with no response.

pricing.description: Computed pricing for the submitted request. Present on settlement_failed only.

DuplicatePaymentBody.description: Returned at HTTP 409 when a payment is replayed within the settlement TTL.
